raw_response:
I have farmed long enough to know I do best when I keep the wheat-maize rotation as the backbone of my land and only leave a smaller part for cash crops that need more hands. My family has some off-farm work, so I will not spread myself too thin on crops that need too much picking and watching. I have well irrigation, so I will use that to protect yield on the wheat-maize land first, because grain keeps the farm steady. I will still plant some chili and cotton for cash, but I will keep them to a size I can manage. On wheat and maize, I will use improved or hybrid seed and put in enough fertilizer to hold yields on my soil. On chili and cotton, I will spend a bit more on crop protection because they are more easily hurt by insects and disease. For tillage, I will keep things simple: rotary tillage on most land because it fits my labor and machinery situation, and I will push for reliable output rather than taking risks.
